canonical_statement: Let n >= 1, let Omega be a bounded domain in R^n, let u be continuous on the closure of Omega and twice continuously differentiable in Omega, and let A(x) be symmetric positive definite. If trace(A(x) D^2 u(x)) >= f(x) in Omega and u <= 0 on the boundary, then sup_Omega u is at most C_n diam(Omega) times the L^n norm, over the upper contact set of u, of f^-(x)/(det A(x))^(1/n), for a constant C_n depending only on n.
domain_and_universes: n : Nat with 1 <= n; Omega : Set (Fin n -> Real); u f : (Fin n -> Real) -> Real; A : (Fin n -> Real) -> Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) Real; Prop in Lean universe 0
quantifiers: bounded open connected Omega subset R^n
u continuous on closure Omega and C^2 on Omega
f measurable with the displayed weighted negative part in L^n
A pointwise symmetric positive definite with sufficient measurability
hypotheses: trace(A(x) * Hessian u(x)) >= f(x) for x in Omega
u(x) <= 0 for x in frontier Omega
A(x) is symmetric positive definite for x in Omega
conclusion: sup_{x in Omega} u(x) <= C_n * diam(Omega) * ||f^- / (det A)^(1/n)||_{L^n(contact_set(u))}

excluded_degenerate_cases: Dimension zero is excluded. If Omega is empty or sup u <= 0, the estimate is trivial but must be handled explicitly. Drift and zeroth-order terms are excluded from the root rather than silently absorbed into the constant.
